Stage 1 · Java foundations

Programs & How They Think

What a program is, and the input → process → output pattern behind every app you love.

⏱ 10 min🧠 No experience needed🧪 Interactive
Step 1

Instructions a literal robot can follow

Programs are exact instructions plus the data they work on.

📝

Think of a recipe card. Ingredients = data, steps = instructions, cook = computer. Vague steps (“add some salt”) work for humans — and fail for machines.

Your music app, bank app, and games are all programs: input (taps, files) → process (calculate, decide) → output (screen, sound). Same pattern, everywhere.

Step 2

One program, three jobs

Predict, then run the lab.

ProgramRead each line in order
public class Main {
  public static void main(String[] args) {
    int a = 4;              // input data
    int b = 5;              // input data
    int sum = a + b;        // process: add
    System.out.println(sum); // output: 9
  }
}

Two stored numbers, one addition, one print. The instructions stay fixed — only the data changes.

Input · a, b
4, 5
Stored data
Process · a + b
9
Calculated
Output
9
Printed
Fixed instructions, changing data — run it again mentally with 100 + 200.
